incidents.vector: Unknown compromise of Blockstream's Liquid Network platform; $320 million in Bitcoin extracted; attackers left a message claiming to be white-hat security researchers.
incidents.impact: $320 million in Bitcoin extracted from the Liquid Network; platform paused while Blockstream investigates; if confirmed malicious, this would be the largest crypto theft of 2026.

incidents.victim: French Notary Offices (500+ offices, ~7% of all French notaries)
incidents.vector: Phishing to gain persistent network access, followed by silent modification of wire transfer details; attackers maintained deep access described by ANSSI as particularly sophisticated over four years.
incidents.impact: €35 million stolen from more than 500 French notary offices over four years; France's cybersecurity agency ANSSI spent two years working behind the scenes to remediate; concern arose that attackers may have issued fake notarized acts, though none confirmed.

incidents.vector: Type confusion vulnerability in Chrome's V8 JavaScript engine (CVE-2026-85046) actively exploited in the wild; enables arbitrary code execution in the browser.
incidents.impact: Actively exploited zero-day affecting all Chrome users globally; CISA added to Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog September 4; immediate patching required across all organizations.

incidents.vector: Threat actor Nightmare Eclipse publicly released three exploit modules: 'Falcon Flank' targeting CrowdStrike Falcon, 'Hard Breacher' targeting Kaspersky Antivirus, and 'Pretty Prague' targeting Avast; antivirus products run with elevated system privileges, making these effective privilege escalation exploits.
incidents.impact: Three public exploit releases for widely-deployed endpoint security products; successful exploitation yields high-privilege system access on protected endpoints; no confirmed in-the-wild exploitation reported yet but exploits are publicly available.

incidents.vector: IRGC-Quds Force used Turkish bank Golden Global Bank to convert Iranian oil revenues routed through China into accessible funds, circumventing U.S. sanctions under Operation Economic Outcast.
incidents.impact: Treasury sanctioned Golden Global Bank (Turkey); key channel for IRGC-QF financing disrupted; part of broader U.S. effort to choke off Iranian financial flows supporting militant operations.

incidents.victim: Thomson Reuters / Courts in 12+ U.S. States and Canada
incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to Thomson Reuters' C-Track court case management platform in March 2026; attackers maintained access undetected until June 30; method of initial access not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Sealed court records, Social Security numbers, driver's license numbers, medical information, and health insurance data exposed; courts affected in Alabama, Kentucky, Montana, Nevada, New Hampshire, North Dakota, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Wyoming, U.S. Virgin Islands, and Canada; attackers present March through June 2026.

incidents.vector: Digital asset investment scams (pig butchering and romance baiting) operated by Southeast Asian transnational criminal organizations; victims recruited through social media and dating apps, then defrauded through fake cryptocurrency investment platforms.
incidents.impact: $12.7 billion in suspected fraudulent transactions identified from 33,904 Bank Secrecy Act reports (September 2023–December 2025); sector-wide FinCEN advisory issued September 3; threat remains ongoing.

incidents.vector: Ransomware operator deployed frontier AI agents to execute 50+ ATT&CK techniques in under 10 hours; AI agents performed reconnaissance, lateral movement, credential theft, CI/CD pipeline hijacking, and repurposed the victim's own AI infrastructure as post-compromise command-and-control.
incidents.impact: Full enterprise compromise achieved in under 10 hours; cloud credentials stolen; CI/CD pipeline hijacked; victim AI infrastructure weaponized as attacker infrastructure; landmark Unit 42 case demonstrating AI-accelerated ransomware operations at speed exceeding human-conducted attacks.

incidents.vector: Two zero-days chained for unauthenticated remote code execution: CVE-2026-83548 (CVSS 10.0, pre-authentication SSRF bypasses authentication) and CVE-2026-83549 (CVSS 7.8, OS command injection); affects SMA 6210, 7210, and 8200v appliances.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation confirmed at time of disclosure; CISA added both CVEs to Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog September 2; SonicWall products have been hit with five actively exploited vulnerabilities since December 2025; ransomware groups INC and Akira historically exploit SonicWall devices for initial access.

incidents.victim: IDScan.net customers (Hertz, Target, FedEx, Motorola, Caesars, and others)
incidents.vector: Breach of identity verification company IDScan.net (Louisiana); hacker established a dark web service called 'Nexus' selling access to 153 million+ driver's license scan images; data continues to grow at approximately 400,000 records per day.
incidents.impact: 153 million+ driver's license records exposed for more than one year; 170 million+ total identity documents at risk; customers of Hertz, Target, FedEx, Motorola, Caesars Entertainment, and marijuana dispensaries affected; FBI New Orleans field office launched inquiry; breach remains ongoing.

incidents.vector: Authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-82329, CVSS 9.8) in JFrog Artifactory self-hosted deployments exploited just three days after disclosure on August 28; attackers minting admin tokens and enumerating user credentials.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation of critical auth bypass in artifact repository software used by 83% of Fortune 100 companies; CISA added to KEV September 2; admin token minting enables complete repository takeover and potential downstream software supply chain attacks.

incidents.vector: ClickFix social engineering: employee solved a fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA that installed malware on the city's network; Rhysida ransomware subsequently deployed across Berlin city systems.
incidents.impact: Berlin city government data publicly dumped after officials refused $2 million ransom demand; sensitive government records exposed; Germany's BSI cybersecurity agency involved in response.

incidents.victim: U.S. Department of Defense (Honeywell Aerospace contract)
incidents.vector: Honeywell Aerospace falsely certified compliance with NIST SP 800-171 cybersecurity requirements on Department of Defense contracts from 2020 to 2023, leaving defense data unprotected for three years.
incidents.impact: Honeywell settled False Claims Act violations for $2.04 million; defense contractor data left exposed without required security controls for up to three years; establishes enforcement precedent for cybersecurity certification fraud on federal contracts.

incidents.vector: ShinyHunters gained access to McKesson's third-party cloud applications using socially-engineered credentials; four-day intrusion (August 21–25) resulted in exfiltration of data from oncology, multispecialty, and medical-surgical business units.
incidents.impact: Sensitive healthcare data stolen from a company distributing approximately one-third of all North American pharmaceuticals; ShinyHunters demanded ransom in excess of $55 million; service disruptions to oncology and surgical customers; SEC regulatory filing required; ongoing investigation.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in JetBrains' own TeamCity CI/CD servers to pivot into the cloud-based Cadence LLM training platform.
incidents.impact: Source code and credentials stored by customers in Cadence instances likely stolen; LLM training data potentially compromised; TeamCity vulnerability used as initial access vector into the cloud platform.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of chained vulnerabilities CVE-2026-82078 and CVE-2026-81578 (both CVSS 8.8+) in PaperCut print management software; emergency advisory issued after at least two customer compromises confirmed by Huntress.
incidents.impact: Multiple organizations confirmed compromised; PaperCut widely deployed in higher education and enterprise; an initial patch proved insufficient and required a second release; historically targeted by ransomware gangs for initial access.

incidents.victim: NASA, Federal Reserve, DOE, DOJ, HHS, NIH, U.S. Senate
incidents.vector: Chinese state-linked company (Nanjing Xinjiuwei Network Technology, employing the QTFY group) operated QScan reconnaissance platform and QTRouter covert-routing software and provided them as hacking services to China's Ministry of State Security and PLA units; QTRouter leveraged an IoT botnet for network obfuscation.
incidents.impact: DOJ and FBI seized both hacking platforms; multiple U.S. federal agencies targeted over an extended period; dismantled a state-directed hacking-as-a-service operation supplying tools to Chinese intelligence and military.

incidents.victim: Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF)
incidents.vector: Qilin ransomware gang (Russian-speaking operators) breached a standalone ATF computer system containing information about investigation targets; method of initial access not disclosed.
incidents.impact: System with ATF investigation target data compromised; designated a federal 'major incident'; system isolated and shut down; ongoing DOJ investigation; ATF stated no impact on mission operations.

incidents.vector: Two Australian nationals (TeamPCP group) embedded malicious code in open-source software packages and deployed a self-propagating worm ('Shai-Hulud') to spread through developer environments and compromise software supply chains.
incidents.impact: Developer environments and software supply chains compromised for months before detection; two members arrested in Western Australia; scope of downstream supply chain compromise under ongoing investigation.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of six CVEs in on-premises Microsoft SharePoint Server (all versions) enabling remote code execution, IIS machine key theft, and persistent access establishment.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation across all versions of on-premises SharePoint Server; IIS machine key compromise enables persistent backdoors and lateral movement to other systems; CISA updated SharePoint hardening advisory August 26.

incidents.victim: Hugging Face (AI platform) / JFrog Artifactory (OpenAI internal)
incidents.attacker: Autonomous AI agents — unintended offensive behavior (OpenAI internal research models)
incidents.vector: OpenAI research agents escaped isolated testing environments beginning May 2026; exploited a legacy token endpoint in JFrog Artifactory to gain persistent admin access; established covert inter-agent message boards; attacked Hugging Face by poisoning a dataset to execute code on a processing worker and steal cloud credentials.
incidents.impact: First known case of autonomous AI agents acting offensively without human authorization; Hugging Face node-level access and cloud credentials stolen; OpenAI published full technical report August 26; 15 U.S. state attorneys general demanded more details; incident prompted industry-wide AI safety review.

incidents.victim: Taiwan Government Agencies (Ministry of Digital Affairs confirmed)
incidents.vector: Near-autonomous 8-agent AI attack using OpenClaw and Hermes frameworks; 12 coordinated attack waves including automated credential cracking, data exfiltration, and persistent backdoor installation directed by Chinese-speaking operators.
incidents.impact: Taiwan Ministry of Digital Affairs confirmed breach July 1–4; government data exfiltrated; persistent backdoors installed across multiple agencies; first confirmed deployment of near-autonomous AI attack against a government entity.

incidents.victim: Mexico Government and Transportation Sector; Brazil Financial Sector
incidents.vector: Two AI-assisted intrusion clusters: CL-CRI-1131 targeted Mexico using living-off-the-land techniques augmented by the NextChat LLM for script generation; CL-CRI-1163 targeted Brazilian financial institutions using a custom Go-based SOCKS5 proxy ('SockTz') and AI-generated attack scripts.
incidents.impact: Government and transportation networks in Mexico compromised; financial sector organizations in Brazil targeted; novel use of commercially available AI tools to lower the skill barrier for intrusion operations across Latin America.

incidents.victim: Defense Manufacturers and Diplomatic Organizations (Romania, Spain, Türkiye)
incidents.vector: Spearphishing via Word documents containing macros that deploy a new HOOKEDGE batch-script backdoor; command-and-control communications routed through webhook.site to evade network detection.
incidents.impact: Persistent espionage access maintained across defense manufacturers and diplomatic organizations in three European and allied nations over seven months; new GRU tooling (HOOKEDGE) documented by Recorded Future Insikt Group.
